entries.title: SqliteConnector permits copying an owned database handle
entries.status: Source-reviewed candidate; not reproduced in running C++
entries.trigger: Copy an open connector and destroy both copies.
entries.issue: The implicit copy duplicates db_ without ownership transfer; both destructors call sqlite3_close_v2 on the same handle. Assignment also loses the previous handle.
entries.proposed_fix: Delete copy operations and provide explicit move ownership if needed.
entries.rust_handling: SQLite connector port has not started. Planned implementation uses rusqlite ownership, bound values, quoted identifiers and checked row/column APIs; no implemented correction or native test is claimed.

entries.title: SqliteConnector does not close a handle when opening fails
entries.status: Source-reviewed candidate; not reproduced in running C++
entries.trigger: Construct a connector for a missing read-only database or an inaccessible path.
entries.issue: sqlite3_open_v2 may return an allocated error handle. The constructor stores it then throws; the object destructor is not run, leaving that handle unclosed.
entries.proposed_fix: Close any returned handle before throwing, or use an owning local guard until successful construction.

entries.title: SQLite bound statements leak on bind or step errors
entries.status: Source-reviewed candidate; not reproduced in running C++
entries.trigger: Supply more blobs than placeholders, or violate a UNIQUE constraint during the step.
entries.issue: Both error branches throw before sqlite3_finalize; the source TODO acknowledges the leak. The statement may also retain borrowed SQLITE_STATIC buffers.
entries.proposed_fix: Use a statement RAII guard on all exits; bind owned data or ensure it outlives the statement.

entries.title: SQLite table-name helpers interpolate names as SQL syntax
entries.status: Source-reviewed candidate; not reproduced in running C++
entries.trigger: Create a table whose name contains an apostrophe or SQL punctuation, then query it by its actual name.
entries.issue: tableExists inserts the name into a quoted literal without escaping; countTableRows and columnExists insert an unquoted identifier. Valid names can fail or alter the query meaning.
entries.proposed_fix: Bind values such as sqlite_master.name and correctly quote SQL identifiers with doubled double quotes.

entries.title: SQLite query helpers ignore step errors and can leak statements
entries.status: Source-reviewed candidate; not reproduced in running C++
entries.trigger: Cause sqlite3_step to return SQLITE_BUSY or another error while querying an existing table.
entries.issue: The helpers inspect column types without checking the step result. Existence queries can conflate an execution error with absence; countTableRows throws on NULL before finalizing. Reachable lock/error behavior still needs execution.
entries.proposed_fix: Check SQLITE_ROW/DONE explicitly, report other statuses, and finalize through RAII.

entries.title: SQLite string extraction truncates embedded NUL bytes
entries.status: Source-reviewed candidate; not reproduced in running C++
entries.trigger: Extract a SQLite TEXT value containing bytes a, NUL, b.
entries.issue: The helper constructs std::string from a C string and loses bytes after the first NUL.
entries.proposed_fix: Use sqlite3_column_bytes with the returned pointer and retain an explicit byte length.

entries.title: SQLite integer-to-string extraction narrows to 32 bits
entries.status: Source-reviewed candidate; not reproduced in running C++
entries.trigger: Read the SQLite INTEGER value 4294967297 through extractValueIntStr.
entries.issue: The helper uses sqlite3_column_int despite SQLite INTEGER being signed 64-bit; conversion to text follows an already narrowed value.
